title: Preparation of Mica Supported Lipid Bilayers for High Resolution Optical Microscopy Imaging
protocol: Place No. 1½ (0.17 mm) coverslips into a staining rack.
Sonicate the coverslips for 30 minutes in 2% detergent at 60 °C.
Wash the coverslips 20 times with deionized water.
Remove the coverslips using forceps and blow dry using compressed air or nitrogen.
Cut mica sheet into 10 x 10 mm square pieces using scissors or a razor blade.
Cut each mica piece into 2-3 thinner leaflets using a razor blade.
Clean a microscopic glass slide with ethanol.
Glue a leaflet of mica to the glass slide using optical adhesive.
Cure the glued assembly under a UV lamp for 10 minutes.
Expose a clean mica surface by removing the first few layers with Scotch tape.
Place a small drop (~20 μm) of high viscosity optical adhesive onto the exposed mica surface.
Gently place a freshly cleaned coverslip onto the drop of adhesive, avoiding air bubbles.
Let the assembly settle for 1 minute.
Cure the assembly under a UV lamp for 10 minutes.
Using an exacto knife, gently dismount the coverslip from side glass slide.
Check the surface quality by naked eye or under a dissecting microscope.
Remove rubber seal from a 1.5 ml vial cap and glue the cap upside down to the surface using optical adhesive or nail polish.
Cure with UV lamp or let air dry for 10 min, respectively.
Place freshly prepared liposome solution into chamber with surface for SLB formation.
Proceed with SLB formation using desired protocol.
Incubate the chamber during imaging to maintain temperature required for lipid stability.
